title: Our travel insurance partner | EC Assets
description: The specialist broker behind the travel and incoming insurance in EC Assets packages: decades of experience with students, au-pairs and travellers, and award-winning service.

blocks.html: The travel health insurance that covers your first weeks in Germany comes from a specialist broker for stays abroad.
Students, language students, au-pairs, researchers and business travellers: the company has built its products around people who are temporarily in a country that is not their own.
The broker designs and manages insurance for foreign guests in Germany and for Germans abroad, and handles advice, contracts and claims with its own team.

blocks.text: What to look for in private cover

blocks.html: Two things matter when comparing private insurance for a stay abroad, according to our partner:

items.html: You fall ill and need medication
You damage something in your rented flat

blocks.html:
Some of this is unpredictable, which is why the partner recommends combining health, liability and accident cover.
A few details worth checking:

items.html: Whether the policy covers outpatient and inpatient treatment and medically necessary rehabilitation.
Whether accident cover includes death and disability.
Whether liability cover includes personal injury, property damage and damage to rented property. Many landlords in Germany require the last of these.

blocks.html: 2. Germany and the other Schengen states set their own insurance requirements, based on EU regulation and German residence law. The minimum insured sum is €30,000; unlimited cover for medical costs is recommended.
The incoming insurance plans offered through our partner meet these requirements.
Complaints to the insurance ombudsman must be submitted in text form, for example by letter or email.
